headline: DepEd Flags ₱2.15-Billion Recovery Need for More Than 9,500 Damaged Classrooms
seoTitle: DepEd Flags ₱2.15B Recovery Need for Damaged Classrooms | FMB News
seoDescription: An approved FMB News brief reports that 9,540 classrooms were damaged by recent monsoon flooding, with DepEd estimating ₱2.15 billion in recovery needs.
deck: DepEd's consolidated assessment in the approved newsroom brief puts the damaged-classroom count above 9,500 and the recovery requirement at ₱2.15 billion.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The approved FMB News morning brief reports that the Department of Education identified 9,540 public-school classrooms damaged by recent monsoon flooding and severe weather, with an estimated ₱2.15 billion needed for emergency rehabilitation.
The brief says temporary learning spaces and Quick Response Fund resources are part of the immediate continuity plan while damaged facilities are assessed and repaired.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Flood and storm damage can affect classrooms well beyond the period of class suspension through electrical, structural, sanitation and furnishing damage. Temporary learning arrangements are used when buildings cannot safely reopen immediately.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The scale of the reported damage affects both education continuity and local reconstruction capacity, particularly in communities repeatedly exposed to flooding.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch DepEd and its Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Service for the final validated damage inventory, regional breakdown, repair schedule and funding releases.
